To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The neutron electric form factor is small and negative at high Q^2 and the proton electric form factor is large and positive at high Q^3.

(a) The neutron electric form factor is consistent with zero within experimental uncertainty, (b) The neutron electric to magnetic ratio is consistent with the value predicted by the quark model, and (c) The proton electric form factor is nonzero at low four momentum transfers and is consistent with zero at large momentum transfers.
the electric form factor of the neutron is not zero and the electric form factor for both the neutron and proton is not constant at high momentum transfer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nucleon electromagnetic form factors and the nucleon spin structure.
the study of the electromagnetic properties of the nucleon.
the study of the nucleon structure using the spin degrees of freedom of the nucleon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neutron form factors are still not known to sufficient precision and the proton form factors are known to sufficient precision but with large uncertainties in the small-x region.
the nucleon form factors are well determined up to a scale of 2 GeV, but that at higher momentum transfers there is a need for new experiments.
the neutron electric form-factor data are not yet in a state where they can be used to constrain the nucleon form-factor models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have measured the proton electric form factor at low Q2 and the neutron electric form factor at intermediate Q2.
we have demonstrated that spin dependent observables are sensitive probes of nucleon form factors and have provided the first experimental access to the neutron electric form factor in this region.
we have shown the feasibility of measuring the electric form factor of the proton and neutron using double polarization experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electric form factors are not zero.
the neutron electric form factor can be extracted from the spin asymmetries in polarized electron scattering off a polarized target.
we can measure the nucleon form factors with high precision and accuracy using double polarization measurements.
